claim: In its simplest form, BER consists of removal of U by UDG to generate an abasic (AP) site.
source: In its simplest form, BER consists of a concerted series of reactions: removal of U by a Uracil-DNA Glycosylase (UDG, UNG in mammals) to generate an abasic (AP) site; scission of the AP site by apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) to generate a nick with a 3'OH and a 5' deoxyribophosphate (5'dRP); insertion of the complementary base and removal of the 5'dRP by polymerase β (Polβ); ligation of the nick by DNA Ligase I or Ligase III-XRCC1 (Beard et al., 2006; Robertson et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the BER pathway, supported by citations.

claim: APE1 cleaves the AP site to generate a nick with a 3'OH and a 5' deoxyribophosphate (5'dRP).

evidence: This is established knowledge about the BER pathway, supported by citations.

claim: Overexpressing NEIL2 in MDA-MB-453 cells doubled the U/G repair-induced mutation rate.
source: And finally, overexpressing NEIL2 in the low-NEIL2 expression cell line, MDA-MB-453, doubled the U/G repair-induced mutation rate (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by mutation rate data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: There is a positive correlation between U/G repair-induced mutations and relative NEIL2 expression in four breast cancer cell lines.
source: In addition, we found a positive correlation between U/G repair-induced mutations and the relative NEIL2 expression (qRT-PCR data) in the four breast cancer cell lines (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Expression of exogenous A3B generated a statistically significant increase in γH2AX foci in Hs578T cells.
source: Expression of exogenous A3B generated a statistically significant increase in γH2AX foci, which was markedly decreased in NEIL2-depleted Hs578T cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A3B-induced γH2AX foci were markedly decreased in NEIL2-depleted Hs578T cells.
source: Expression of exogenous A3B generated a statistically significant increase in γH2AX foci, which was markedly decreased in NEIL2-depleted Hs578T cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A3B deaminase activity was unaffected in NEIL2-depleted Hs578T cell lines.
source: This was not the result of diminished deaminase activity as A3B deaminase activity generated from the A3B-HA expression vector was unaffected in NEIL2-depleted cell lines (Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro deaminase assay data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Rescue of NEIL2 with exogenous NEIL2-HA restored A3B-induced γH2AX foci in NEIL2-depleted Hs578T cells.
source: Rescue of NEIL2 with exogenous NEIL2-HA (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) restored A3B-induced γH2AX foci in NEIL2-depleted cells (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Expression of NEIL2-HA in MDA-MB-453 cells increased A3B-mediated γH2AX foci.
source: Furthermore, similar to U/G repair-induced mutagenesis (Figure 2F), expression of NEIL2-HA in non-mutagenic MDA-MB-453 cells increased A3B-mediated γH2AX foci (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: NEIL2 is involved in A3B-induced genomic DNA damage.
source: These results indicate that NEIL2 is involved in A3B-induced genomic DNA damage.
evidence: This is inferred from the collective experimental results showing NEIL2's role in A3B-mediated effects.

claim: NEIL2 exhibited robust glycosylase/lyase activity on hydroxyl-U-containing single-stranded oligonucleotide.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Hazra et al., 2002), NEIL2 exhibited robust glycosylase/lyase activity on hydroxyl-U-containing single-stranded oligonucleotide (ssDNA-OHU), but only trace activity on double-stranded oligonucleotide (dsDNA-OHU/G) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NEIL2 exhibited only trace activity on hydroxyl-U-containing double-stranded oligonucleotide.
source: Consistent with previous studies (Hazra et al., 2002), NEIL2 exhibited robust glycosylase/lyase activity on hydroxyl-U-containing single-stranded oligonucleotide (ssDNA-OHU), but only trace activity on double-stranded oligonucleotide (dsDNA-OHU/G) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NEIL2 was inactive on both ssDNA-U and dsDNA-U/G.
source: Furthermore, NEIL2 was inactive on both ssDNA-U and dsDNA-U/G (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The NEIL2 lyase can cleave AP sites generated by UDG from U-containing oligonucleotides.
source: However, the NEIL2 lyase can cleave the AP sites (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) generated by UDG from U-containing oligonucleotides (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and 1D.

claim: APE1 is the conventional BER AP lyase.
source: APE1 is the conventional BER AP lyase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the BER pathway.

claim: APE1 generates 3'OH-terminated fragments.
source: APE1 and NEIL2 generate respectively 3'OH and 3'P-terminated fragments (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), which migrate differently on Urea-PAGE (Schomacher et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about APE1's enzymatic product, supported by citation.

claim: NEIL2 generates 3'P-terminated fragments.
source: APE1 and NEIL2 generate respectively 3'OH and 3'P-terminated fragments (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), which migrate differently on Urea-PAGE (Schomacher et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about NEIL2's enzymatic product, supported by citation.

claim: 3'OH and 3'P-terminated fragments migrate differently on Urea-PAGE.
source: APE1 and NEIL2 generate respectively 3'OH and 3'P-terminated fragments (Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 2), which migrate differently on Urea-PAGE (Schomacher et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: In a reaction with both NEIL2 and APE1, the NEIL2 product prevailed over the APE1 product.
source: In a reaction with both NEIL2 and APE1, the NEIL2 product prevailed over the APE1 product (lane 5 of Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro competition assay data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: NEIL2 generated an unexplained double-band product from dsDNA-U/G oligonucleotides in the concentration gradient assay.
source: In contrast to its activity on ssDNA, NEIL2 generated an unexplained double-band product from the dsDNA-U/G oligonucleotides in the concentration gradient assay (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is an observation from experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Double band NEIL2 products have been previously observed.
source: Double band NEIL2 products have been previously observed (Hazra et al., 2002) and in our case were related to the length and composition of the substrate (35 nt, Figure 4C and 51nt, Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous literature, supported by citation.

claim: The amount of NEIL2 products increased with increasing levels of NEIL2 when APE1 was somewhat limiting.
source: When APE1 was somewhat limiting (0.005U, Low APE1 panel, lanes 4–8, Figure 4D), the amount of NEIL2 products increased with increasing levels of NEIL2.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro competition assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: NEIL2 products prevailed even with excess APE1.
source: Notably, the same results were found with excess APE1 (0.02U, High APE1 panel, lanes 9–13, Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro competition assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: NEIL2 supplants APE1 at AP sites.
source: These results strongly suggest that NEIL2 supplants APE1 at AP sites.
evidence: This is inferred from the competition assay results.

claim: The Polβ reaction is a rate-limiting step during BER.
source: As the Polβ reaction is a rate-limiting step during BER (Srivastava et al., 1998), we compared the NEIL2 and APE1 products as substrates for this reaction using His-tagged Polβ purified from E. coli (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Polβ showed robust activity on the APE1 product.
source: Although Polβ showed robust activity on the APE1 product (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B), it was less active on the NEIL2 product, which depended on PNKP (Figure 4E and illustration in Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro Polβ incorporation assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4B.

claim: Polβ was less active on the NEIL2 product, which depended on PNKP.
source: Although Polβ showed robust activity on the APE1 product (Figure 4—figure supplement 4B), it was less active on the NEIL2 product, which depended on PNKP (Figure 4E and illustration in Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro Polβ incorporation assay data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Polβ incorporation was attenuated by NEIL2.
source: As expected from the usurpation of AP sites by NEIL2 (Figure 4B,D), Polβ incorporation was attenuated by NEIL2 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro Polβ incorporation assay data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The cleavage product generated from the substrate by Fpg yielded a 3'-32P-terminated product that was equally susceptible to the phosphatase activity of either PNKP or T4 polynucleotide kinase.
source: As a positive control, the cleavage product generated from this substrate by the E. coli bifunctional glycosylase, Fpg, yielded a 3'-32P-terminated product that was equally susceptible to the phosphatase activity of either PNKP or T4 polynucleotide kinase (Figure 4—figure supplement 4E).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro phosphatase assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4E.

claim: The internally-labeled substrate was resistant to complete cleavage by NEIL2.
source: However, in contrast to the complete cleavage of this substrate by Fpg and to NEIL2's complete cleavage of a 5'-terminally labeled substrate (Figure 4B–D and Figure 4—figure supplement 3B,C), the internally-labeled substrate was resistant to complete cleavage by NEIL2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 4E, lanes 4 and 5).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4E.

claim: The incomplete cleavage of internally-labeled substrate by NEIL2 may reflect an isotope effect on NEIL2 activity.
source: Perhaps these results reflect an isotope effect on NEIL2 activity.
evidence: This is speculation based on the observed experimental results.

claim: Exo1 siRNA knockdown reduced production of γH2AX foci in Hs578T cells.
source: Exo1 siRNA knockdown (Figure 5A) reduced production of γH2AX foci in Hs578T cells but had no effect in the NEIL2-stable-knockdown cell lines (Figure 5B,C), indicating that Exo1 activity occurs downstream of NEIL2.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: Exo1 knockdown had no effect on γH2AX foci in NEIL2-stable-knockdown cell lines.
source: Exo1 siRNA knockdown (Figure 5A) reduced production of γH2AX foci in Hs578T cells but had no effect in the NEIL2-stable-knockdown cell lines (Figure 5B,C), indicating that Exo1 activity occurs downstream of NEIL2.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: Exo1 activity occurs downstream of NEIL2.
source: Exo1 siRNA knockdown (Figure 5A) reduced production of γH2AX foci in Hs578T cells but had no effect in the NEIL2-stable-knockdown cell lines (Figure 5B,C), indicating that Exo1 activity occurs downstream of NEIL2.
evidence: This is inferred from the epistasis analysis showing Exo1 knockdown has no additional effect in NEIL2-depleted cells.

claim: U/G repair-induced mutations were decreased in Exo1-knockdown Hs578T cells.
source: In addition, U/G repair-induced mutations were also decreased in Exo1-knockdown Hs578T cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by mutation rate data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Knockdown of Exo1 recapitulated the effects of NEIL2 knockdown.
source: Thus, knockdown of Exo1 recapitulated the effects of NEIL2 knockdown.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar phenotypes observed upon knockdown of either gene.

claim: The nicked AP products generated by APE1 or NEIL2 were equally good substrates for Exo1.
source: Furthermore, the nicked AP products generated by APE1 or NEIL2 were equally good substrates for Exo1 despite the different 5' termini of the nicked DNA (Figure 5E, 5'dRP for APE1 and 5'P for NEIL2).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro Exo1 nuclease assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: NEIL2 can divert a BER intermediate to an Exo1-generated single-stranded DNA that is susceptible to A3B deaminase activity, DSBs, or other DNA damage.
source: These results indicate that NEIL2 can divert a BER intermediate to an Exo1-generated single-stranded DNA that is susceptible to A3B deaminase activity, DSBs, or other DNA damage (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion inferred from the collective experimental results.

claim: Elevated expression of NEIL2 sensitizes Hs578T breast cancer cells to A3B-mediated mutations.
source: A major unresolved issue in cancer biology is why some cancers become vulnerable to the mutagenic effect of A3 single-stranded deaminases (Alexandrov et al., 2013b; Cescon et al., 2015; Helleday et al., 2014; Petljak et al., 2019; Roberts and Gordenin, 2014), and even more intriguing, that it can be sporadic over clonal lineages of the same tumor (Petljak et al., 2019). Although it may be unlikely that a single mechanism would explain every instance of A3-mediated mutations in cancers, we report here that elevated expression of the bifunctional glycosylase, NEIL2 (Figure 2A), sensitizes Hs578T breast cancer cells to two A3B-mediated effects, repair-induced mutations (Figure 2B–F) and DNA damage revealed by γH2AX foci (Burns et al., 2013a; Landry et al., 2011) (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Elevated expression of NEIL2 sensitizes Hs578T breast cancer cells to A3B-mediated DNA damage revealed by γH2AX foci.
source: A major unresolved issue in cancer biology is why some cancers become vulnerable to the mutagenic effect of A3 single-stranded deaminases (Alexandrov et al., 2013b; Cescon et al., 2015; Helleday et al., 2014; Petljak et al., 2019; Roberts and Gordenin, 2014), and even more intriguing, that it can be sporadic over clonal lineages of the same tumor (Petljak et al., 2019). Although it may be unlikely that a single mechanism would explain every instance of A3-mediated mutations in cancers, we report here that elevated expression of the bifunctional glycosylase, NEIL2 (Figure 2A), sensitizes Hs578T breast cancer cells to two A3B-mediated effects, repair-induced mutations (Figure 2B–F) and DNA damage revealed by γH2AX foci (Burns et al., 2013a; Landry et al., 2011) (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: NEIL2 depletion mitigates both A3B-mediated mutations and DNA damage.
source: NEIL2 depletion mitigates both effects, but they are induced by its overexpression.
evidence: This is supported by knockdown and overexpression experiments shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: A3B-mediated mutations and DNA damage are induced by NEIL2 overexpression.
source: NEIL2 depletion mitigates both effects, but they are induced by its overexpression.
evidence: This is supported by overexpression experiments shown in Figures 2F and 3D.

claim: NEIL2 is unable to process U/G mismatches.
source: In vitro BER experiments using purified components show that NEIL2, though unable to process U/G mismatches, subverts the BER process that repairs these lesions by usurping the normal BER endonuclease, APE1, at AP sites (the first BER product) (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro enzymatic assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: NEIL2 subverts the BER process by usurping APE1 at AP sites.
source: In vitro BER experiments using purified components show that NEIL2, though unable to process U/G mismatches, subverts the BER process that repairs these lesions by usurping the normal BER endonuclease, APE1, at AP sites (the first BER product) (Figure 4).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro competition assay data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The NEIL2 scission product is vulnerable to the 5'−3' exonuclease Exo1.
source: Although we have not determined why the NEIL2 scission product is a poor substrate for Polβ, the important issue is that it is vulnerable to the 5'−3' exonuclease Exo1 (Figure 5E), which generates single-stranded DNA susceptible to A3 deaminases.
evidence: This is supported by in vitro Exo1 nuclease assay data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Exo1 generates single-stranded DNA susceptible to A3 deaminases.
source: Although we have not determined why the NEIL2 scission product is a poor substrate for Polβ, the important issue is that it is vulnerable to the 5'−3' exonuclease Exo1 (Figure 5E), which generates single-stranded DNA susceptible to A3 deaminases.
evidence: This is inferred from the known substrate specificity of A3 deaminases and the Exo1 activity.

claim: Exo1 and NEIL2 double-knockdown mimics the effect of NEIL2 depletion.
source: In vivo experiments show that Exo1 and NEIL2 double-knockdown mimics the effect of NEIL2 depletion, indicating that NEIL2 acts upstream of Exo1 (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is supported by epistasis analysis data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: NEIL2 acts upstream of Exo1.
source: In vivo experiments show that Exo1 and NEIL2 double-knockdown mimics the effect of NEIL2 depletion, indicating that NEIL2 acts upstream of Exo1 (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is inferred from the epistasis analysis.

claim: The most parsimonious explanation is that NEIL2 diverts BER to Exo1-generation of single-stranded DNA that would be vulnerable to A3B deaminase.
source: Therefore, the most parsimonious explanation of our results is that NEIL2 diverts BER to Exo1-generation of single-stranded DNA that would be vulnerable to A3B deaminase (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the collective experimental results.

claim: The eventual outcome at a given AP site is not likely to be only a function of the relative intracellular concentrations of each protein.
source: It is also important to stress that the eventual outcome at a given AP site is not likely to be only a function of the relative intracellular concentrations of each protein.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the complexity of cellular processes.

claim: APE1 has other binding partners.
source: APE1 does have other binding partners (Bazlekowa-Karaban et al., 2019; Madlener et al., 2013; Tell et al., 2009; Thakur et al., 2014) and we presume this is likely also to be true of NEIL2 (Das et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: NEIL2 likely has other binding partners.
source: APE1 does have other binding partners (Bazlekowa-Karaban et al., 2019; Madlener et al., 2013; Tell et al., 2009; Thakur et al., 2014) and we presume this is likely also to be true of NEIL2 (Das et al., 2007).
evidence: This is speculation based on analogy to APE1 and supported by citation.

claim: NEIL2, even at a concentration of APE1 that is in four-fold excess, can enzymatically outcompete APE1.
source: In addition, our results shows that NEIL2, even at a concentration of APE1 that is in four-fold excess of the amount needed to completely digest an AP site, can enzymatically outcompete APE1 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by in vitro competition assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the promoter region of NEIL2 affect its expression.
source: Several papers reported the presence of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the promoter region of NEIL2 that affected its expression (Benítez-Buelga et al., 2017; Kinslow et al., 2008; Kinslow et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous literature, supported by citations.

claim: Only MDA-MB-453 contained a SNP (rs804271) in the NEIL2 promoter region among the four cell lines studied.
source: We sequenced the 700 bp NEIL2 promoter region of the four cell lines that we used, and only the non-mutagenic, low NEIL2-exspressing MDA-MB-453 contained a SNP (rs804271) that had been previously correlated with elevated NEIL2 expression and DNA damage in a BRCA1/2 background (Benítez-Buelga et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by sequencing data from the study.

claim: SNP rs804271 had been previously correlated with elevated NEIL2 expression and DNA damage in a BRCA1/2 background.
source: We sequenced the 700 bp NEIL2 promoter region of the four cell lines that we used, and only the non-mutagenic, low NEIL2-exspressing MDA-MB-453 contained a SNP (rs804271) that had been previously correlated with elevated NEIL2 expression and DNA damage in a BRCA1/2 background (Benítez-Buelga et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous literature, supported by citation.

claim: Additional factors contribute to the regulation of NEIL2 in these cells.
source: Thus, additional factors contribute to the regulation of NEIL2 in these cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that the SNP pattern does not explain the NEIL2 expression pattern.

claim: Clonal lineages of MDA-MB-453 can undergo sporadic episodes of A3-mediated mutations.
source: Interestingly, it was recently reported that clonal lineages of MDA-MB-453 can undergo sporadic episodes of A3-mediated mutations (Petljak et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge from recent literature, supported by citation.

claim: The ATCC isolate of MDA-MB-453 (HTB-131) was in a low mutation phase.
source: Thus, it seems that our ATCC isolate of this line (HTB-131) was in a low mutation phase.
evidence: This is inferred from the low mutation rate observed in the study and the known sporadic nature of mutations in this line.
